naming.rule: Package versions and architectural line names are separate. Enhanced descendants of v1 remain on the v1 line; v2 names are reserved for the alternate ledger architecture, which lost all seven rounds and is retired.

round_history.reason: Candidate A did not change project-building modules; candidate B failed architecture review; hybrids were not built.
The improved v1 and B+A each passed 1/3. B+A failed the no-worse-regression prerequisite, so the fully gated v1 line won.
v1.3.1 and A+B each passed 2/3, but v1.3.1 had lower total provider cost; v2.2 and B+A passed 1/3. All winner release gates passed.
v1.4 passed 3/3 and every release gate; A+B and B+A passed 2/3, v2.4 passed 1/3. The selected base remains the enhanced v1 line.
v1.6 passed 3/3 with the lowest current-round cost and time among perfect candidates and passed every release, provenance, frozen-workload, wheel, Docker, and system-E2E gate; B+A passed 1/3.
v1.7 passed 2/3 and all five new critical provenance/sandbox gates; v2.7 and B+A passed 1/3. The v1.7 generator remained byte-identical to v1.6 and every release gate passed.

v1.8 passed 3/3 generation attempts and 11/11 frozen operational tests against the incumbent's 2/11, at the lowest cost and wall time of the round. v2.9 passed 0/3 and B+A passed 2/3. A+B was not materialized because B produced no transferable advantage.

loop_status.reason: The v2 ledger line lost all seven rounds and the Duplicate Finder workload reached 3/3, so it can no longer discriminate between candidates. That workload records only the Python standard library in component_decisions, so it never exercised the reuse-first composition path the product is built around.
loop_status.successor_measures: Assembly of real evidence-backed components behind declared contracts, which is the capability the retired benchmark could not measure.
